props.title: Holy Smoke
props.initialSlug: A cult expert meets his match in a headstrong woman

sections.content: Jane Campion's Holy Smoke stands as a provocative exploration of spiritual manipulation and sexual power dynamics, featuring Kate Winslet as Ruth, a young Australian woman who falls under the spell of an Indian guru, and Harvey Keitel as PJ Waters, the American "cult deprogrammer" hired to break her faith. The film follows similar thematic territory as other '90s films examining religious devotion and manipulation like Safe (1995) and Breaking the Waves (1996), but Campion's distinct feminist lens turns the traditional power dynamic on its head.

sections.content: Campion's signature visual style, developed in The Piano (1993) and Portrait of a Lady (1996), transforms the Australian outback into a surreal psychological battleground. The desert setting recalls other Australian New Wave classics like Walkabout (1971) and Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975), where the landscape becomes a character itself, challenging Western notions of civilization and control.

The film's exploration of gender dynamics and religious devotion connects to later works like Under the Banner of Heaven (2022) and Midsommar (2019), though Campion's approach is more intimate and psychosexual. The power struggle between Ruth and PJ becomes increasingly complex as traditional roles of deprogrammer/victim blur into a more nuanced examination of faith, desire, and manipulation. sections.content: Like other films in Campion's oeuvre, particularly In the Cut (2003) and The Power of the Dog (2021), Holy Smoke subverts traditional gender roles and power structures. The film's third act, where PJ dons a red dress and experiences a psychological breakdown, represents a radical departure from conventional depictions of masculine authority, especially in the context of religious or spiritual leadership.
